brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut: they keep 5.9% profit vs 3.8% for similar firms — there's room to share that margin with us.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% price cut on rigid plastic packaging
priceAsk.target: Target roughly ₹0.65–0.80/pc for typical caps (28 mm induction-wad PP cap)
priceAsk.basis: The market ask for this item is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with the verdict 'MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec'. They keep 5.9% profit vs 3.8% for similar firms — that extra margin can come back to us.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (moving from 30 days to 15 days after receipt) in exchange for a price cut equal to their borrowing rate of 12.19%
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹22.57 L of cash for us, but they borrow money at 12.19%, so paying early is worth that rate to them — trade it for a matching price cut.

brief.financialLeverage: They're financially healthy — CRISIL A+ / Stable rating, not losing money, and their revenue is ₹937.60 Cr. But their cash is stuck for 104d vs 79d for similar firms, so cash is tight for them and they'll value faster payment. We're only 0.59% of their revenue, so we're small to them — but they're growing fast and want volume. Lead with the price cut (they have the margin: 5.9% vs 3.8%), then offer quicker payment as a sweetener if they meet our target price.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter, does pharma bottles and caps, revenue ₹2569.83 Cr, health B (65/100) — the top second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers and pharma — strong and profitable, a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd
alternates.why: Listed PET bottle and jar specialist (Pearlpet brand) — direct fit for PET bottles.

risks: We're only 0.59% of their revenue — we have little volume leverage, so lead with the margin gap (5.9% vs 3.8%) and the market price band, not just our size.
Their health score is B (64/100) and Altman Z is 2.17 (grey zone) — they're not in distress, but not rock-solid either. Don't squeeze so hard you destabilize a key packaging supplier.
They pay their own suppliers slower than most (49d vs 37d) — so asking for longer payment terms from them won't fly; the play is faster payment from us in exchange for a price cut.
The market ask verdict says 'MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom' — there's room to negotiate down to ₹0.65–0.80, but going much lower may hit a floor unless we commit serious volume or relax specs.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We've benchmarked your pricing against the open market — there's headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 per cap at volume, and your profit margin runs higher than similar firms, so let's talk about a 10–15% price cut and how we can help your cash flow in return.
